---
title: "Alternative input data"
subtitle: "How the Java results change when national maps are replaced by global datasets"
---

```{ojs}
import {withDownload, adminMarks, cellFeatures, fmt, pearson} from "../assets/js/dl.js"
runs = FileAttachment("data/alternatives/runs.csv").csv({typed: true})
years = FileAttachment("data/alternatives/years.csv").csv({typed: true})
cells = FileAttachment("data/alternatives/cells.csv").csv({typed: true})
waterMaps = FileAttachment("data/alternatives/water_maps.csv").csv({typed: true})
outline = FileAttachment("data/java_outline.geojson").json()
provinces = FileAttachment("data/provinces.geojson").json()
districtsGeo = FileAttachment("data/districts.geojson").json()
base = runs.find(d => d.variant === "baseline")
variants = runs.filter(d => d.variant !== "baseline")
groups = ["crop mask", "water regime", "soil", "weather"]
dark = document.body.classList.contains("quarto-dark")
// categorical slots 1-3 (validated all-pairs, light and dark) and a neutral for the national run
slots = dark ? ["#3987e5", "#d95926", "#199e70"] : ["#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a"]
neutral = dark ? "#c3c2b7" : "#52514e"
// the two ends of the PuOr scheme the site's other difference maps use
lessColor = dark ? "#f1a340" : "#c4620c"
moreColor = dark ? "#998ec3" : "#5e3c99"
mapW = Math.min(width, 900)
yearRange = `${d3.min(years, d => d.season_year)}-${d3.max(years, d => d.season_year)}`
```

The Java case study uses national data where it exists: the ATR/BPN rice field map (2024) as the crop mask
and the Ministry of Agriculture irrigation map as the water regime. This page shows how the simulated results
change when global datasets take their place, as they would in an area without national data. How each dataset
is prepared is described in [Input data](../xdssat/data.qmd).

Each run changes **one input** and keeps the others of the national run. All runs: Jawa, agricultural years
${yearRange}, uniform calendar (wet season 15 November, dry season 1 April for irrigated rice), IR 58,
140 kg N, SLPF 1. SLPF 1 is the uncalibrated model, so the levels are higher than reported yields; the
differences between runs are what this page shows. Crop outside a water regime map is rainfed
(`treatments > default_regime`).

```{ojs}
Inputs.table(runs.map(d => ({
  "Input changed": d.group, "Run": d.label, "Source": d.source,
  "Rice area, M ha": d.ha / 1e6, "Irrigated, M ha": d.ha_irrigated / 1e6, "Weather cells": d.cells,
  "Production, Mt/yr": d.production_t / 1e6, "Change": d.production_t_change_pct,
  "Failed seasons": d.failed
})), {format: {"Rice area, M ha": fmt.d2, "Irrigated, M ha": fmt.d2, "Production, Mt/yr": fmt.d1,
  "Change": d => d === 0 ? "" : `${d > 0 ? "+" : ""}${d.toFixed(1)}%`}, layout: "auto", rows: 12})
```

## How much production changes

Mean simulated production per year (dry grain), each run against the national run:

```{ojs}
barRows = groups.flatMap(g => variants.filter(d => d.group === g))
  .map(d => ({...d, row: `${d.group}: ${d.label} (${d.production_t_change_pct > 0 ? "+" : ""}${d.production_t_change_pct.toFixed(1)}%)`}))
changeBars = withDownload(Plot.plot({
  width: Math.min(width, 860), height: 60 + barRows.length * 34, marginLeft: 300, marginRight: 20,
  x: {label: "Change in production from the national run, %", grid: true},
  y: {label: null, domain: barRows.map(d => d.row)},
  color: {domain: ["less", "more"], range: [lessColor, moreColor], legend: true, label: "Production against the national run"},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(barRows, {x: "production_t_change_pct", y: "row", insetTop: 6, insetBottom: 6, rx: 4,
      fill: d => d.production_t_change_pct < 0 ? "less" : "more",
      title: d => `${d.label}\n${fmt.d1(d.production_t / 1e6)} Mt/yr against ${fmt.d1(base.production_t / 1e6)}\nirrigated ${fmt.d2(d.ha_irrigated / 1e6)} M ha, rainfed ${fmt.d2(d.ha_rainfed / 1e6)} M ha`,
      tip: true}),
    Plot.ruleX([0], {stroke: neutral})
  ]
}), "xdssat-alternatives-production-change")
```

```{ojs}
byGroup = Object.fromEntries(groups.map(g => [g, variants.filter(d => d.group === g)]))
pct = (v) => `${v > 0 ? "+" : ""}${v.toFixed(1)}%`
extreme = (g) => byGroup[g].reduce((a, b) => Math.abs(b.production_t_change_pct) > Math.abs(a.production_t_change_pct) ? b : a)
cropText = byGroup["crop mask"].map(d => `${d.label} ${pct(d.production_t_change_pct)}`).join(", ")
waterText = byGroup["water regime"].map(d => `${d.label} ${pct(d.production_t_change_pct)}`).join(", ")
soilText = byGroup["soil"].map(d => `${d.label} ${pct(d.production_t_change_pct)}`).join(", ")
weatherText = byGroup["weather"].map(d => `${d.label} ${pct(d.production_t_change_pct)}`).join(", ")
```

- **Crop mask** sets where rice is simulated and how much: ${cropText}.
- **Water regime** sets the irrigated area, and only irrigated rice is planted in the dry season:
  ${waterText}.
- **Soil**: ${soilText}.
- **Weather grid**: ${weatherText}.

## Production per year

Simulated production of both seasons per agricultural year, the national run (grey) against the runs of each
kind of input:

```{ojs}
annual = d3.rollups(years, v => d3.sum(v, d => d.production_t) / 1e6, d => d.variant, d => d.season_year)
  .flatMap(([v, ys]) => ys.map(([y, p]) => ({variant: v, season_year: y, mt: p})))
labelOf = new Map(runs.map(d => [d.variant, d.label]))
yearPlot = (g) => {
  const vs = ["baseline", ...byGroup[g].map(d => d.variant)];
  const rows = annual.filter(d => vs.includes(d.variant)).map(d => ({...d, label: labelOf.get(d.variant)}));
  const last = d3.max(rows, d => d.season_year);
  // end labels: keep at least 7% of the value range between neighbours
  const ends = rows.filter(d => d.season_year === last).map(d => ({...d, ly: d.mt})).sort((a, b) => a.mt - b.mt);
  const [lo, hi] = d3.extent(rows, d => d.mt);
  const gap = (hi - lo) * 0.07;
  for (let i = 1; i < ends.length; i++) if (ends[i].ly - ends[i - 1].ly < gap) ends[i].ly = ends[i - 1].ly + gap;
  return withDownload(Plot.plot({
    width: Math.min(width, 430), height: 250, marginLeft: 45, marginRight: 150,
    x: {label: "Agricultural year", tickFormat: d => String(d)},
    y: {label: "Production, Mt", grid: true},
    color: {domain: vs.map(v => labelOf.get(v)), range: [neutral, ...slots], legend: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.lineY(rows, {x: "season_year", y: "mt", stroke: "label", strokeWidth: 2, tip: true}),
      Plot.text(ends, {x: "season_year", y: "ly", text: "label", dx: 6, textAnchor: "start", fill: "currentColor"})
    ]
  }), `xdssat-alternatives-years-${g.replace(" ", "-")}`);
}
html`<div class="grid">${groups.map(g => html`<div class="g-col-12 g-col-md-6"><h4>${g}</h4>${yearPlot(g)}</div>`)}</div>`
```

## Where the difference is

Mean production per year in each weather cell, the selected run minus the national run (on the selected run's
own grid; for the 0.25° weather, the national run summed into its cells):

```{ojs}
viewof pick = Inputs.select(new Map(variants.map(d => [`${d.group}: ${d.label}`, d.variant])), {label: "Run"})
```

```{ojs}
diffMap = {
  const rows = cells.filter(d => d.variant === pick);
  const half = rows[0].grid_deg / 2;
  const m = d3.quantile(rows.map(d => Math.abs(d.diff_t)).sort(d3.ascending), 0.95) || 1;
  const r = runs.find(d => d.variant === pick);
  return withDownload(Plot.plot({
    width: mapW, height: Math.round(mapW * 0.42),
    projection: {type: "mercator", domain: outline},
    caption: `${r.label} minus the national run: ${fmt.d1(r.production_t / 1e6)} against ${fmt.d1(base.production_t / 1e6)} Mt per year`,
    color: {type: "diverging", scheme: "PuOr", pivot: 0, domain: [-m, m], clamp: true, legend: true,
      label: "Difference in production per year, t (purple: more, orange: less)"},
    marks: [
      Plot.geo(provinces, {fill: dark ? "#2b2b2a" : "#f1f1f1", clip: true}),
      Plot.geo(cellFeatures(rows, half).features, Plot.centroid({fill: d => d.properties.diff_t,
        title: d => `cell ${d.properties.lat.toFixed(2)}, ${d.properties.lon.toFixed(2)}\nnational ${fmt.int(d.properties.baseline_t)} t/yr\nthis run ${fmt.int(d.properties.production_t)} t/yr\ndifference ${fmt.int(d.properties.diff_t)} t/yr`,
        tip: true})),
      ...adminMarks(Plot, provinces, districtsGeo)
    ]
  }), `xdssat-alternatives-diff-${pick}`);
}
```

The input itself for the selected run, in the same cells: rice area for a crop mask, irrigated share of the
rice for a water regime, and production per year for soil and weather:

```{ojs}
inputMap = {
  const r = runs.find(d => d.variant === pick);
  const rows = cells.filter(d => d.variant === pick && d.crop_ha > 0);
  const half = rows[0].grid_deg / 2;
  const kind = r.group === "crop mask" ? "area" : r.group === "water regime" ? "share" : "production";
  const val = kind === "area" ? (d => d.crop_ha) : kind === "share" ? (d => d.irrigated_ha / d.crop_ha) : (d => d.production_t);
  const color = kind === "share"
    ? {type: "linear", scheme: "BuGn", domain: [0, 1], legend: true, label: "Irrigated share of the cell's rice", tickFormat: ".0%"}
    : kind === "area"
      ? {type: "sqrt", scheme: "YlGn", legend: true, label: "Rice area in the cell, ha"}
      : {type: "sqrt", scheme: "YlGn", legend: true, label: "Production per year, t"};
  return withDownload(Plot.plot({
    width: mapW, height: Math.round(mapW * 0.42),
    projection: {type: "mercator", domain: outline},
    color,
    marks: [
      Plot.geo(provinces, {fill: dark ? "#2b2b2a" : "#f1f1f1", clip: true}),
      Plot.geo(cellFeatures(rows.map(d => ({...d, v: val(d)})), half).features, Plot.centroid({fill: d => d.properties.v,
        title: d => `cell ${d.properties.lat.toFixed(2)}, ${d.properties.lon.toFixed(2)}\n${kind === "share" ? fmt.pct(d.properties.v) : fmt.int(d.properties.v)}`,
        tip: true})),
      ...adminMarks(Plot, provinces, districtsGeo)
    ]
  }), `xdssat-alternatives-input-${pick}`);
}
```

## The inputs compared

### Crop mask

```{ojs}
cellKey = (d) => `${d.lat.toFixed(2)},${d.lon.toFixed(2)}`
baseCells = new Map(cells.filter(d => d.variant === "baseline").map(d => [cellKey(d), d.crop_ha]))
maskRows = byGroup["crop mask"].map(r => {
  const own = new Map(cells.filter(d => d.variant === r.variant).map(d => [cellKey(d), d.crop_ha]));
  const keys = [...new Set([...baseCells.keys(), ...own.keys()])];
  return {"Crop mask": r.label, "Source": r.source, "Rice area, M ha": r.ha / 1e6, "Weather cells": r.cells,
    "Correlation of the area per cell with ATR/BPN": pearson(keys.map(k => baseCells.get(k) ?? 0), keys.map(k => own.get(k) ?? 0))};
})
Inputs.table([{"Crop mask": base.label, "Source": "ATR/BPN rice fields 2024", "Rice area, M ha": base.ha / 1e6,
  "Weather cells": base.cells, "Correlation of the area per cell with ATR/BPN": 1}, ...maskRows],
  {format: {"Rice area, M ha": fmt.d2, "Correlation of the area per cell with ATR/BPN": fmt.d2}, layout: "auto"})
```

A general cropland class does not say which crop grows there: with WorldCover or MODIS, rice is simulated on
all cropland. MODIS counts cropland/natural vegetation mosaics as well. MapSPAM is specific to rice, but it
places reported areas with an allocation model on a 9 km grid.

### Water regime

Rice area of the ATR/BPN map by class of the Ministry of Agriculture map and of the other two water regime
maps, million ha:

```{ojs}
waterTable = (map) => {
  const cls = [...new Set(waterMaps.filter(d => d.map === map).map(d => d.cls))];
  return ["irrigated", "rainfed"].map(m => Object.fromEntries([["Ministry of Agriculture", m],
    ...cls.map(c => [`${map}: ${c}`, (waterMaps.find(d => d.map === map && d.moa === m && d.cls === c)?.ha ?? 0) / 1e6])]));
}
tableFormat = (rows) => Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(rows[0]).slice(1).map(k => [k, fmt.d2]))
lgAgree = {
  const w = waterMaps.filter(d => d.map === "LGRIP30" && (d.cls === "irrigated" || d.cls === "rainfed"));
  return d3.sum(w.filter(d => d.cls === d.moa), d => d.ha) / d3.sum(w, d => d.ha);
}
lgCover = {
  const w = waterMaps.filter(d => d.map === "LGRIP30");
  return d3.sum(w.filter(d => d.cls === "irrigated" || d.cls === "rainfed"), d => d.ha) / d3.sum(w, d => d.ha);
}
lgAgreeText = fmt.pct(lgAgree)
lgCoverText = fmt.pct(lgCover)
```

```{ojs}
Inputs.table(waterTable("LGRIP30"), {format: tableFormat(waterTable("LGRIP30")), layout: "auto"})
```

```{ojs}
Inputs.table(waterTable("MapSPAM"), {format: tableFormat(waterTable("MapSPAM")), layout: "auto"})
```

Where LGRIP30 has cropland (${lgCoverText} of the rice area), it agrees with the Ministry of Agriculture map on
${lgAgreeText} of the area. Neither map is ground truth, so this measures agreement, not accuracy; the LGRIP30
user guide reports 79.2% overall accuracy for Southeast Asia. LGRIP30 counts a cropland as irrigated with "at
least one artificial irrigation during the crop growing period".

### Soil and weather

The soil runs replace the SoilGrids profiles of every cell: SoilGrids without the organic carbon factors fitted
to WISE profiles, and one generic profile for all of Java (the IRRI soil of the template, or an HC27 loam).
The weather run uses AgERA5 regridded to 0.25° (an area mean for rain), so a weather cell holds about six times
the area and its soil is the crop-weighted mean of the larger cell.

## Reproduce

```bash
python docs/scripts/run_alternatives.py --list    # the runs and the prepared inputs each needs
python docs/scripts/run_alternatives.py           # all runs
python docs/scripts/export_alternatives.py        # writes docs/java/data/alternatives/
```

Each run's experiment file is written next to its results (`<cache>/runs/alternatives/<run>.yml`); the inputs
are prepared as described in [Input data](../xdssat/data.qmd).
